paragraph: Angola's National Institute of Quality Infrastructure was [formed by Presidential Decree 95/21 of 20 April 2021](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2021/decreto-presidencial-n-o-95-21-de-20-de-abril/>). The decree gives it the job of developing, publishing and approving Angolan standards. The institute [made its 2026 catalogue available on 9 March 2026](<https://iniq.gov.ao/2026/03/13/%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%8d%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%90-%f0%9d%90%83%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%92%f0%9d%90%8f%f0%9d%90%8e%f0%9d%90%8d%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%81%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%8b%f0%9d%90%88%f0%9d%90%99/>), with 140 new national standards. The announcement names no standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

On 29 August 2025 Burundi's Bureau burundais de normalisation et de contrôle de la qualité [signed a memorandum in Bujumbura with the Office congolais de contrôle](<https://bankable.africa/fr/climat-des-affaires/0109-1626-commerce-rdc-burundi-vers-une-reduction-des-barrieres-non-tarifaires>), its counterpart in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The memorandum covers cooperation in standardisation, quality control and certification. The international standards organisation's member page describes the bureau as an [incorporated administrative public institution whose aims include preparing draft national standards](<https://www.iso.org/member/1591.html>). Neither source names a standard on information technology or data that the bureau has issued. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Benin's Agence nationale de Normalisation, de Métrologie et du Contrôle Qualité [was established by Order 2017-031 of 23 January 2017](<https://www.iso.org/member/308845.html>), according to the international standards organisation's member record. It is a public institution under the Ministry of Industry, with the mandate to manage the national standardisation and certification systems. The record names no national standard on information technology or data. It names no scheme for certifying an organisation against one, and no organisation the agency has certified. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

[Decree 2016-357 of 13 May 2016](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/bkf165557.pdf>) approves the statutes of Burkina Faso's Agence Burkinabè de Normalisation, de la Métrologie et de la Qualité as a public administrative establishment. It charges the agency with drawing up and issuing national standards. On 4 February 2026 the agency [signed a framework convention with the telecoms regulator](<https://abnorm.bf/2026/02/05/signature-de-la-convention-cadre-pour-la-gestion-des-identifiants-dobjets-oid/>) on managing object identifiers. Neither text names a national standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Botswana Bureau of Standards was established by [the Standards Act of 1995, which commenced on 1 August 1996](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/bot91763.pdf>). It publishes [an annual work programme of standards projects](<https://bobstandards.bw/standards-annual-work-programme/>); issue 341, updated on 16 April 2026, covers April 2026 to March 2027. In November 2025 the trade minister [told Parliament](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/89185>) that the bureau had developed voluntary national standards on school uniforms. None of the three sources names a standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Cameroon's Agence des Normes et de la Qualité, ANOR, is described on the [international standards organisation's member page](<https://www.iso.org/member/1623.html>), as at 16 October 2026, as responsible for developing and certifying standards. That page is the one statement of the body's role found. It names no national standard on information technology or data, and no certification against one. It gives no law or decree that set the body up. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Office congolais de contrôle was created by Ordinance No. 74-013 of 1974, says [ISO's member page for the office](<https://www.iso.org/member/308894.html>), dated 2026. The page describes it as the country's national body for metrology, standardisation and certification. It names no national standard on information technology or data that the office has issued or adopted. It names no certification against one, and no public body that the office has certified. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Law No. 19-2015 of 29 October 2015 created the Agence Congolaise de Normalisation et de la Qualité, known as ACONOQ. The international standards organisation's [member page](<https://www.iso.org/member/11493926.html>) calls it the national standardization body. The page says the agency manages the national standards register. It names no standard on information technology or data that the agency has issued. It records no certification offered by the agency. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

In October 2026 the economy minister said that the president had [recently signed a decree setting up the Office comorien de la normalisation et de la métrologie](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/office-national-de-la-normalisation-i-un-projet-de-loi-sur-la-qualit%C3%A9-en-voie-de-validation.html>) in Comoros. It is the national standards and metrology body. The report names no standard on information technology or data, and no certification scheme for either. It is the only source found on the office, so no earlier position can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Cabo Verde's Instituto de Gestão da Qualidade e da Propriedade Intelectual publishes [the list of Cabo Verdean standards](<https://igqpi.cv/download/158/acervo-normativo/8119/lista-de-ncv-2.pdf>), updated in March 2024. The list runs from NCV 001:2015 to NCV 025:2023. None of its 25 national standards is on information technology, information security, software or data. Certificates held by a port company, a data centre and the state's digital agency against international standards name neither the institute nor a certifier accredited in the country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Djibouti's Agence Djiboutienne des Normes et de la Qualité was [created by a law of 7 January 2021](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n100-an-20-8eme-l-portantes-creation-de-lagence-djiboutienne-des-normes-et-de-la-qualite/>) as the national reference body for drawing up standards. [A decree of 4 May 2022](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/decret-n2022-092-pr-mct-portant-organisation-et-fonctionnement-de-lagence-djiboutienne-des-normes-et-de-la-qualite/>) organises it. The Council of Ministers of 13 January 2026 [examined its 2026 budget of 134.9 million Djibouti francs](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2026-01-13>), and recorded two technical committees made operational in 2025, for agri-food products and for electrical and household appliances. No standard on information technology or data is named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Algeria's Algerian Institute of Standardisation, IANOR, was [created by executive decree 98-69 of 21 February 1998](<https://www.ianor.dz/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/2-D_exe_98-69_instituant-IANOR-FR.pdf>) to draw up and publish Algerian standards. Its [draft national standardisation programme for 2026](<https://www.ianor.dz/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/PROJET-DE-PROGRAMME-NATIONAL-DE-NORMALISATION-2026.pdf>), published in February 2026, lists the revision of national standard NA 13037. The revision brings it up to the 2025 edition of the international standard on comparing and ordering character strings in information technology. Neither text names certification against it or an organisation certified. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

On 1 October 2025 the Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality endorsed [Egyptian Standard 7982-1/2025](<https://www.eos.org.eg/en/standard/14180>), which adopts the international standard on the exchange of electricity metering data. Its register classes the standard under information technology, and it is not obligatory. The organisation states that it is [the sole official body for preparing and issuing Egyptian standards](<https://www.eos.org.eg/ar/page/11>). The register entry names no certifier and no organisation certified against the standard. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

Eritrea's Eritrean Standards Institution was [established by Proclamation No. 75 of 1995](<https://www.ecolex.org/details/legislation/proclamation-to-provide-for-the-establishment-of-the-eritrean-standards-institution-no-75-of-1995-lex-faoc203313/>) as the sole national organ for standardisation, quality assurance and metrology. The proclamation gives it the power to prepare compulsory Eritrean Standards. The international standards organisation's member record [gives 446 national standards published](<https://www.iso.org/member/318778.html>). The proclamation names no standard on information technology or data, and no source found names a scheme for certifying against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

On 24 April 2026 the Ethiopian Standards Board [officially approved 5 mandatory cybersecurity standards and 31 guidelines and frameworks](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/information-network-security-administration_insa-digitalethiopia2030-cybersecurity-activity-7453356614822277120-hb2m>). The Information Network Security Administration drafted them with the Ethiopian Standards Institute. In the last twelve months this is the new position. No earlier national standard on information technology or data has been found. [In October 2026 the institute held a database of more than 11,000 standards](<https://addisfortune.news/authorities-bid-for-digital-quality-sparks-fury-among-cash-strapped-businesses>). The announcement names no certifier and no organisation certified against the new standards. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

Gabon's national standardization body, the Agence Gabonaise de Normalisation, AGANOR, was [created by decree 0227/PR/MIMT of 23 June 2014](<https://aganor.ga/aganor/a-propos-de-laganor/>), with power to draw up, approve and publish Gabonese standards. The agency's page lists certification among its services. It names no standard on information technology or data that an organisation could be certified against, and names no certified organisation. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Ghana's [Ghana Standards Authority Act, 2022](<https://ghalii.org/akn/gh/act/2022/1078>), Act 1078, was assented to and published in the Gazette on 30 June 2022. On 19 March 2026 the authority [hosted a steering committee meeting](<https://gsa.gov.gh/2026/03/gsa-hosts-steering-committee-meeting-on-national-metrology-institute-ii-project/>) on the second phase of a metrology institute project with Germany's metrology institute. None of the sources found names a national standard on information technology or data. The Act's citation and history, the only part found, name no certification scheme. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

[A presidential decree read on national television on 7 January 2023](<https://guineenews.org/2023/01/07/decret-les-attributions-lorganisation-de-institut-guineen-de-normalisation-et-de-metrologie-fixes/>) fixes the attributions, organisation and operation of Guinea's Institut Guinéen de Normalisation et de Métrologie. It is a public administrative body under the industry and finance ministries. The decree charges it with drafting national standards, or adopting foreign or international ones, and with publishing them. The report names no standard on information technology or data that the institute has issued. It names no scheme for certifying an organisation against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Gambia Standards Bureau's [2022 catalogue](<https://tgsb.gm/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/TGSB-STANDARDS-CATALOGUE-2022.pdf>) lists GAMS ISO/IEC 27001:2005, on information security management systems, as a Gambian Standard adopted from the international one. The same document says the bureau [was established by an Act of Parliament in 2010](<https://tgsb.gm/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/TGSB-STANDARDS-CATALOGUE-2022.pdf>) and provides conformity assessment services. It names no certification scheme for the standard and no organisation certified against it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

Kenya's standards body is the Kenya Bureau of Standards. It [was established by the Standards Act, Chapter 496, and started operations in July 1974](<https://www.iso.org/member/1854.html>). In the last twelve months, in November 2026, a law firm's analysis said [the bureau has issued KS 3007, a Code of Practice for AI Applications](<https://cioafrica.co/ai-governance-fragmentation-cause-for-concern/>). It is a voluntary national standard. Before then no Kenyan standard on information technology or data had been found. In July 2025 the Kenya Accreditation Service [extended the bureau's accreditation so it can certify organisations to ISO/IEC 27001:2022](<https://blog.kenas.go.ke/empowering-quality-trade-and-digital-security-kenas-accredits-kebs-to-four-strategic-international-standards/>). No source found says that standard is a Kenyan one. None says anyone certifies against KS 3007. Operating would need certification against a Kenyan standard on information technology or data offered in the country.

[An Act to amend the Executive Law and establish the Liberia Standards Authority](<https://www.moci.gov.lr/sites/default/files/documents/An%20Act%20To%20Amend%20The%20Executive%20Law%20Of%20Liberia%20And%20To%20Establish%20The%20Liberia%20Standards%20Authority.pdf>) was published by the commerce ministry on 5 August 2022. [ISO's member page says the authority began work in 2024](<https://www.iso.org/member/11464839.html>) as the national body that develops and maintains Liberian standards. Neither source names a national standard on information technology or data. Neither names a scheme for certifying an organisation against one, or an organisation the authority has certified. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

[ISO's member page](<https://www.iso.org/member/1890.html>) lists Libya's National Centre for Standardization and Metrology as the national standards body. It describes a public organization established in 1990, which issues and approves standards. On 3 February 2026 the centre's supreme committee [adopted its plan for 2026 and a number of Libyan standards](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=350300&lang=ar>). The report of the meeting names none of them as a standard on information technology or data. Neither source names certification against such a standard. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The trade and industry minister [said on 16 September 2020](<http://www.trade.gov.ls/news/official-address-by-the-minister-of-trade-and-industry-honourable-dr-thabiso-molapo-at-the-operationalisation-of-the-lesotho-standards-institution-lsi/>) that the Lesotho Standards Institution was now operational as the country's national standards body. An Act published in 2014 had created it, with a mandate to develop and publish national standards. The minister's address is the only source found on the institution. It names no national standard on information technology or data. It names no certification scheme and no certified organisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Morocco's national standards body is IMANOR, the Institut Marocain de Normalisation, which [ISO's member page](<https://www.iso.org/member/1931.html>) says was created in 2010 to replace SNIMA, the earlier body. The page says IMANOR produces Moroccan standards, and says nothing about certification. Nothing found names a Moroccan standard on information technology or data. Nothing found says IMANOR or a certifier accredited in Morocco offers certification against one. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Madagascar's Bureau des Normes de Madagascar [was created by decree 98-944 of 4 November 1998](<https://www.bnm.mg/description-et-activites/>) and is now governed by decree 2014-1570 of 30 September 2014. A United Nations Development Programme assessment of December 2025 [describes the bureau as the national standards body and a correspondent member of the international standards organisation](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-12/dra_final_report_madagascar_vf_0.pdf>). It says public information shows no specific programme on standards for artificial intelligence or data governance. Neither source names a national standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Mali's Agence Malienne de Normalisation et de Promotion de la Qualité was [created by an ordinance of 19 March 2012](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/mli152386.pdf>) as a public administrative body. In the last twelve months its board, meeting on 29 January 2026, [adopted a 2026 budget of 243.3 million CFA francs](<https://leronier.ml/2026/02/02/14eme-session-ordinaire-du-conseil-dadministration-de-lamanorm-le-projet-de-budget-2026-est-equilibre-en-recettes-et-en-depenses-a-la-somme-de-243-306-303-francs-cfa-contre-318-369-036-francs-c/>), against 318.4 million in 2025. None of the three sources names a national standard on information technology or data. The ordinance names no certification against one. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Mozambique's Instituto Nacional de Normalização e Qualidade was established on 24 March 1993 as the central body coordinating standardisation and quality, says the [ISO member page](<https://www.iso.org/member/1978.html>). [Decree 8/2022 of 14 March 2022](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz211531.pdf>) charges it with implementing Mozambican technical standards and certifying management systems, products, services and people. On 16 March 2026 it [awarded a quality management certificate to the finance area of the National Institute of Health](<https://ins.gov.mz/area-financeira-do-ins-certificada-com-a-norma-iso-90012015/>). No standard or certificate on information technology or data is named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

[Decree 2023-113 of 7 September 2023](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/mau229551.pdf>) says Mauritania's Office National de Normalisation et de Métrologie was instituted by a decree of 9 May 2023. The decree also creates a national council for standardisation and quality promotion under the industry minister, and gives the office its secretariat and that of an accreditation cell. It was published in the official journal of 15 October 2023. It names no national standard on information technology or data, no body accredited to certify and no certification against such a standard. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Under Government Notice 119 of 25 January 2025 the Mauritius Standards Bureau [published five ISO/IEC standards on information technology and cybersecurity as Mauritian Standards](<https://msb.intnet.mu/Documents/Standards/Published%20Mauritian%20Standards/Published%20Mauritian%20Standards%20in%202025.pdf>). The bureau certifies organisations itself. Its register at 31 December 2025 [lists ten certificates, all marked as accredited](<https://msb.intnet.mu/Documents/Attachment%202%20-%20List%20of%20registered%20firms%20ISMS%2031-12-2025.pdf>), six of them held by public bodies. In the last twelve months the count has risen: by 30 June 2026 the register [listed 11 certified organisations](<https://msb.intnet.mu/Documents/Certification-Schemes/General/Registered%20firms/Attachment%202%20-%20List%20of%20registered%20firms%20ISMS%2030-06-2026.pdf>). The Passport and Immigration Office's certificate in that register is dated 30 October 2025.

The Malawi Bureau of Standards [is established by the Malawi Bureau of Standards Act, No. 14 of 2012](<https://portal.trade.gov.mw/en-gb/site/display/48>), assented to on 12 July 2012. Its object is preparing and issuing standards. A certificate dated 14 December 2025 from the Southern African Development Community's accreditation service [accredits the bureau to certify quality management systems](<https://www.sadcas.org/sites/default/files/2026-04/CBAS%20-%20MBS%20-%20Cert%20%26%20SoA%20%28QMS%20Certification%29%20%28Issue%2001%29%20Dec%202025.pdf>). The Act and the certificate name no national standard on information technology or data. They name no accreditation to certify against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Namibian Standards Institution [is established by the Standards Act, 2005](<https://www.nsi.com.na/download/standards-act-18-of-2005/>), signed on 23 December 2005. Its chief executive [said in October 2025](<https://thebrief.com.na/2025/10/namibia-lags-behind-region-with-235-standards-plans-to-develop-1200/>) that it had published 235 standards since it was set up in 2008. A notice of 15 June 2026 [announced four new Namibian Standards](<https://nsi.com.na/officially-developed-namibian-standards-nams-food-products-and-food-safety-management/>), on chilled seafood, dates, laundry processes and the energy performance of refrigerating appliances. No standard on information technology or data is named. The Act names no certification against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Nigeria's Standards Organisation of Nigeria was [established by an Enabling Act of 1971 to prepare standards](<https://www.iso.org/member/1982.html>), says the international standards organisation's member page. That page is the one source found on the body's standing. It names no national standard on information technology or data, and records no certification against one. No source found says that an organisation in Nigeria can be certified against one. No earlier position has been found, so no change can be stated for the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Rwanda Standards Board [is established by Law 50/2013 of 28 June 2013](<https://www.rsb.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Quick_links/Rwanda_Standards_Board_-_RSB.pdf>), with the mission of establishing and publishing voluntary national standards. In October 2025 the international standards organisation said the board [has developed and published more than 4,130 standards](<https://www.iso.org/news/2025/10/iso-arso-kigali-agreement-trade>). On 6 March 2026 the board [signed mutual recognition arrangements](<https://www.rsb.gov.rw/updates/news-detail/rsb-signed-mutual-recognition-arrangements-with-aconoq-and-saz-to-promote-trade-as-arso-joined-to-the-certification-of-local-industries-under-the-acap-programme>) with the standards bodies of Congo and Zimbabwe. No standard on information technology or data is named, and no certification against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organization, [set up in 1993](<https://www.iso.org/member/2078.html>), [publishes an online catalogue of adopted Sudanese Standards](<https://www.ssmo.gov.sd/Content/SectorDetails/783020af-a1ce-46f5-aaa1-525dd82ca005>). The catalogue lists a 2019 standard on the digital repository, a 2016 standard on an application protocol for open systems interconnection and a 2015 standard on managing metadata for records. In July 2026 the organisation was [piloting electronic payment of its standards certification fees](<https://sudanhorizon.com/ssmo-integrates-eisali-payment-service-with-baladna-platform/>) in Khartoum. The report names no certification against a standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

The Sierra Leone Standards Bureau [was created by the Standards Act No 2 of 1996](<https://www.iso.org/member/576517.html>), says the international standards organisation's member page, dated 16 October 2026. The bureau states that its standards department [develops and publishes national standards](<https://slsb.gov.sl/standards-overview/>), and that it has published 204 in the public gazette. Its overview, published in 2023, names a technical committee on information security management systems. It names no national standard on information technology or data that the committee or the bureau has issued. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Somali Bureau of Standards is [a national standards body established by an Act of parliament](<https://www.iso.org/member/8867946.html>), the Somali Standards and Quality Control law, numbered Lr27. The member record, published in August 2026, says the bureau has been operational since early 2020. In May 2023 the US International Trade Administration said the bureau [had adopted 145 standards in various fields over three years](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/somalia-trade-standards>). Neither source names a national standard on information technology or data. The record names no certification scheme and no certified organisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

South Sudan's [National Bureau of Standards Act, 2012](<https://mojca.gov.ss/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/National-Bureau-of-Standards-Act-2012.pdf>) set up the National Bureau of Standards as a body corporate to formulate, adopt and endorse standard specifications as South Sudan standards. The bureau was operating in May 2026, when its technical manager [spoke for it at a World Metrology Day event on 20 May](<https://www.onecitizendaily.com/index.php/2026/05/21/ssnbs-plans-to-tackle-internet-data-bundle-billing-complaints/>). In November 2026 the [government's eServices portal described the bureau](<https://accounts.eservices.gov.ss/mdas>) as the national body for the quality, safety and standardisation of goods and services. The Act names no standard on information technology, software or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

São Tomé and Príncipe's Serviço Nacional da Propriedade Intelectual e da Qualidade is described on its [own site in 2026](<https://senapiq.gov.st/>) as a public institute under the ministry responsible for industry. Its functions include proposing policy on standardisation, certification, accreditation and metrology. The international standards organisation [lists it as a correspondent member](<https://www.iso.org/member/7310132.html>). Neither source cites the law or decree that set it up. Neither names a national standard on information technology or data, or a certification scheme. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

In August 2025 [General Notice No. 79 of 2025](<https://times.co.sz/25189/business/eswatini-issues-19-new-national-standards-across-key-sectors/>), under the Standards and Quality Act, 2023, designated 19 new Eswatini National Standards. They include the National Addressing Standard, SZNS ISO 19160-1:2015 and SZNS ISO 19160-2:2022, on the classes of address and how addresses are assigned. The Eswatini Standards Authority [is established by the Standards and Quality Act](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/swa142025.pdf>), assented to on 8 November 2001. The report of the notice names no certifier for the addressing standard and no organisation certified against it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need certification against such a standard offered in the country, by the standards body or by a certifier accredited there.

The Seychelles Bureau of Standards [is established by the Seychelles Bureau of Standards Act, 2014](<https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/acc_e/syc_e/wtaccsyc52_leg_2.pdf>), assented to on 28 March 2014. It prepares draft standards and declares them Seychelles Standards by notice in the Gazette. The President [appointed an eight-member board for three years from 1 August 2025](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2025-09/Gazette%20No%2064%20-%2029th%20September%202025.pdf>). None of the sources found names a standard on information technology or data. The Act names no scheme for certifying an organisation against one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

On 31 July, 5 August and 7 August 2026 the technical committees of Chad's Agence Tchadienne de Normalisation adopted draft Chadian standards, [as the agency's site records](<https://atnor.td/>). Among them are ten international standards on quality management. None of the drafts is on information technology or data. [The standardisation law](<https://www.atnor.td/la-loi-relative-a-la-normalisation/>) creates the national standardisation structures, among them the agency, and charges it with preparing and issuing Chadian standards. The site names no certification against a standard on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

On 17 and 18 August 2026 Togo's Agence togolaise de normalisation presented in Lomé [46 national standards it drew up](<https://agriculture.gouv.tg/fsrp-togo-46-normes-nationales-et-31-programmes-de-certification-pour-renforcer-la-qualite-et-la-competitivite-des-produits-agroalimentaires/>), all on agri-food value chains such as rice, soya, poultry and meat. The agriculture ministry reports 31 certification programmes for agri-food products beside them. Its account names no standard on information technology or data and no certification against one. It does not say what law or decree set the agency up. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

On 25 May 2026 Tunisia's Institut National de la Normalisation et de la Propriété Industrielle [issued standardisation bulletin no. 441](<http://www.innorpi.tn/sites/default/files/2026-05/Officiel%20EP%20441_0.pdf>), which opened a two-month public enquiry on draft Tunisian standards. The drafts cover measurement, quality management, and electrical and fibre-optic cables. They include no standard on information technology, information security, software or data. In October 2026 [ISO's member registry](<https://www.iso.org/member/2158.html>) describes the institute as a public institution under the Ministry of Industry. No certification against a standard on information technology or data is named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

Tanzania's standards body, the Tanzania Bureau of Standards, was [established by the Standards Act of 1975 and operational from 6 April 1976](<https://www.iso.org/member/2120.html>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the head of the communications regulator [said the bureau has newly introduced a Tanzania Standard on accessibility of communications and ICT products and services for persons with disabilities](<https://dailynews.co.tz/tcra-advances-digital-inclusion-for-pwds-through-assistive-technologies/>). Before then the only position found was a set of draft adoptions of international standards that the bureau [circulated for comment in February 2025](<https://www.tbs.go.tz/uploads/publications/en-1739785468-Stakeholders'%20Comments%20Letter%20Feb%202025.pdf>). The bureau [lists the e-Government Authority as certified to ISO 27001:2022 from 30 January 2026](<https://www.tbs.go.tz/uploads/documents/sw-1787571805-CERTIFIED%20CLIENTS%20UNDER%20ISO%2027001%20ISMS.pdf>). No source says that standard is a Tanzania Standard. Operating would need certification against a Tanzania Standard on information technology or data.

The Uganda National Bureau of Standards was [established by an Act of 1983 and operational since 1989](<https://www.unbs.go.ug/attachments/menus/34/UNBS%20Annual%20Report%20FY%202024-2025.pdf>). It held 4,862 national standards at the end of June 2025. The trade ministry [said in August 2026](<https://www.mtic.go.ug/trade-minister-sanjay-tanna-tasks-unbs-to-improve-efficiency-in-service-delivery/>) that the National Standards Council had reported 551 new standards in the year to June 2026. A notice approved on 16 December 2025 [proposes 15 standards for compulsory declaration](<https://www.unbs.go.ug/attachments/alerts/1/DECLARATION%20NOTICE%20DECEMBER%202025%20-%20Copy.pdf>). None of the standards these sources name is on information technology or data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

South Africa's standards body is the South African Bureau of Standards, whose board acts under the Standards Act of 2008. In the last twelve months, [Notice 3890, gazetted on 17 April 2026](<https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202604/54520gen3890.pdf>), listed a second edition of SANS 19784-1, the national standard on the programming interface for biometric applications. It is listed among revised information technology standards. No source found says the bureau or an accredited certifier offers certification against a national standard on information technology or data. Operating would need such certification on offer in the country.

In August 2026 the Zambia Bureau of Standards said on [its own site](<https://www.zabs.org.zm/standards-development>) that it develops, publishes, maintains and withdraws Zambian National Standards. The site says it has developed standards in sectors that include information and communication technology, and that there are more than 6,500 Zambian National Standards. It names no standard on information technology or data. In September 2026 the bureau [signed a technical cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Standards Board](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/zambia-rwanda-sign-technical-cooperation-agreement-to-harmonise-standards/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a named national standard on information technology or data, issued or adopted as a national standard.

The Standards Association of Zimbabwe [lists ZWS ISO/IEC 27001:2022](<https://www.saz.org.zw/accreditations-2/>), on information security management systems, as a Zimbabwe standard. Its [list of standards published in the first quarter of 2026](<https://www.saz.org.zw/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Q1-published-standards-2026_-002.pdf>) adds national standards on artificial intelligence, cloud security and digital evidence. In the last twelve months its scheme for certifying organisations against the information security standard [was accredited in February 2026](<https://www.saz.org.zw/accreditations-2/>). Its quality, environmental and occupational health schemes were accredited earlier. The page names no organisation certified against it. Mature would need a dated source naming a public body certified in the past three years, by the standards body or an accredited certifier.
